title: 10-Point Website Audit Checklist: Is Your Site Costing You Clients?
excerpt: Most business websites have at least 3 problems that quietly cost them leads. A practical 10-point checklist to audit your site yourself — no specialist tools required.

blocks.text: Your website is either working for you or working against you. There's not much in between.
Most business owners assume their site is fine. It loaded when they last checked. The contact form works. But 'fine' and 'converting visitors into clients' are very different things.
This checklist covers the 10 areas that most frequently cause business websites to underperform — and gives you a concrete way to check each one.
Why You Should Audit Your Site Regularly

A website isn't a one-time project. Google's ranking factors change. Browsers update. Security vulnerabilities emerge. A site that performed well at launch can degrade significantly within 12–18 months without any changes from your side.
A quick audit twice a year catches issues before they compound into lost rankings, lost leads, or a security incident.
The 10-Point Checklist
1. Page Speed
Test your site at PageSpeed Insights (free, from Google). Look at the mobile score — that's the one that affects rankings.

items: **Pass:** Mobile score 80+. Core Web Vitals all green.
**Flag:** Mobile score 50–79. Some metrics amber.
**Fail:** Mobile score below 50. Visitors are leaving before the page loads.

blocks.text: WordPress sites without dedicated optimization typically score 35–65 on mobile. Next.js sites consistently score 90–99.
2. Mobile Responsiveness
Open your site on your phone. Navigate through your service pages, contact page, and blog. Look for:

items: Text that requires pinching to read
Buttons or links too small to tap accurately
Horizontal scrolling (should never happen)
Forms that are hard to fill in on a small screen

blocks.text: Over 60% of B2B website visits now happen on mobile. If your site is uncomfortable to use on a phone, you're losing the majority of your visitors.
3. SEO Basics
Check these elements on your homepage and key landing pages:

items: **Title tag:** Under 60 characters, contains your primary keyword
**Meta description:** Under 160 characters, explains what the page offers
**H1 tag:** One per page, matches the page's topic
**Alt text on images:** Descriptive, not keyword-stuffed
**No duplicate content:** Each page targets a different search intent

blocks.text: 4. Accessibility
Poor accessibility affects SEO and excludes paying customers. Run your site through WAVE (wave.webaim.org) and check for:

items: Missing alt text on images
Insufficient color contrast (text must be readable against its background)
Missing form labels
No skip navigation link for keyboard users

blocks.text: 5. Security
Basic security checks you can do without any technical knowledge:

items: **HTTPS:** Your URL starts with https:// and shows a padlock. If not, Google marks it as insecure.
**No mixed content:** No images or scripts loading over http:// on an https:// page
**CMS and plugins up to date:** If you're on WordPress, outdated plugins are the most common attack vector
**No 'hacked site' warnings in Google Search Console**

blocks.text: 6. Analytics Setup
You can't improve what you don't measure. Check:

items: Google Analytics 4 (or equivalent) is installed and receiving data
Google Search Console is connected
Goals or conversions are configured — not just pageviews
You check your analytics at least monthly

blocks.text: Many businesses have analytics installed but never configured conversions. Without goal tracking, you can't tell which pages and traffic sources actually generate leads.
7. Clear CTAs on Key Pages
Every page should have one clear next step. On your homepage and service pages, ask:

items: Is there a visible CTA above the fold (without scrolling)?
Does every page tell the visitor what to do next?
Are CTAs specific ("Book a free consultation") rather than vague ("Contact us")?
Is the primary CTA repeated at the bottom of long pages?

blocks.text: 8. Content Freshness
Google favors sites that update regularly. Check:

items: Service content is accurate (prices, team, services offered)
Case studies and testimonials are recent (within 2 years)
Blog has content from the last 6 months
No 404 errors on internal links (check via Google Search Console)

blocks.text: 9. Legal Compliance (GDPR)
Especially critical for European businesses:

items: **Privacy policy:** Exists, is current, covers all tools you use (analytics, forms, chatbots)
**Cookie consent:** A proper consent banner before cookies are set — not just an info bar
**Imprint (Impressum):** Required by law in Germany and Austria — must include legal name, address, responsible person
**Contact form data processing:** Users must understand what happens to their data

blocks.text: GDPR violations carry fines up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover. A missing or outdated privacy policy is one of the most common triggers for complaints.
10. Conversion Tracking
Beyond basic analytics, check whether you're tracking what actually matters:

items: Form submissions (contact, quote requests, newsletter signups)
Phone number clicks
Key page visits (pricing page, case study page)
Scroll depth on high-value content

blocks.text: If you're running paid ads, conversion tracking is non-negotiable. Every campaign not tied to a tracked outcome is budget going out with no accountability.
Quick Scorecard

rows: Usable on phone without pinching or horizontal scroll
Title, meta description, H1 on key pages
HTTPS, no mixed content, CMS updated
No outdated info, no broken links

blocks.text: What If You Fail Several Points?
A few red flags is normal — especially for sites older than 2 years. The important thing is knowing where you stand so you can prioritize fixes.
Speed and security are usually the highest-impact fixes. A slow, insecure site loses visitors before they even read your offer.
